controls.label: intercept
controls.help: Line value at x = 0; it shifts both predictions y_hat_i, hence both residuals, both squared residuals and sse.

controls.label: slope
controls.help: Line change per unit x; it sets both predictions y_hat_i, hence both residuals, both squared residuals and sse in proportion to the x_i values.

explorations.title: Slope change alone
explorations.instruction: slope is set to 2, all other controls at their defaults (x_1 = 0, y_1 = 1, x_2 = 2, y_2 = 3, intercept = 0).
explorations.observe: sse rises from 0 at slope = 1 to 8 at slope = 2, with the second squared residual q_2 rising from 0 to 4 and the first squared residual q_1 staying at 1 ... which readouts change under the preset? predictions y_hat_2, residual r_2, squared residual q_2 and sse all change; y_hat_1, r_1 and q_1 do not, because x_1 = 0 removes slope from the first prediction.
explorations.why: Only the second prediction depends on slope because x_1 equals zero, so residual r_2 = y_2 - slope*x_2 falls from 1 to -1 and its square q_2 = 1 grows to 4; sse = q_1 + q_2 therefore goes from 1 + 1 = 2 at the default slope 1 to 1 + 4 = 5 at slope 2, a rise that the sweep line shows as a parabola in slope.

explorations.title: Perfect fit at the two points
explorations.instruction: intercept is set to 1.0 and slope is set to 1.0, with x_1 = 0, y_1 = 1, x_2 = 2, y_2 = 3.
explorations.observe: Both squared residuals q_1 and q_2 become 0 and sse is 0; both bars in the squared-residual chart vanish and the sweep line touches 0 at slope 1.
explorations.why: The line passes through both observations, so r_1 = 1 - (1 + 1*0) = 0 and r_2 = 3 - (1 + 1*2) = 0; the summed squares then vanish. This is the limiting case of a zero loss, not a fit produced by the page.
